questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

We’ve sent a very strong protest letter. That should make them sit up and __take notice__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4 i.e. Consider.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase** "sit up and take notice" **means to pay careful attention to something or someone because they are interesting or important. 

 
 
• **Example:** When the new CEO implemented the innovative policy, it made the whole industry sit up and take notice.
 
 
 
• The word **"Consider" **means to think carefully about something, typically before making a decision. 
 
 
• **Example**: Before buying the house, they considered all its pros and cons.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the **correct answer** is- **Consider.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Follow** means to go or come after a person or thing proceeding ahead. 

 
 
• **Example**: She followed the instructions carefully to assemble the furniture.
 
 
 
• **Attend** means to be present at an event, meeting, or function.
 
 
• **Example**: He attended the conference to gain insights into the latest industry trends.
 
 
 
• **Observe** means to notice or perceive (something) and register it as being significant. 
 
 
• **Example**: The scientist observed the reactions under the microscope carefully.

questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3 i.e. 'second wind'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given phrase **"burst of energy"** refers to a sudden increase in energy or enthusiasm.

 
 
• **Example:** After resting for a while, the marathon runner got a burst of energy and was able to finish the race.
 
 
 
• The correct idiom **"second wind**" means finding new strength or energy to continue after becoming tired or discouraged. 
 
 
• **Example:** Just when I was about to give up on the project, I found my second wind and managed to complete it on time.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is- Second wind.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **"A fancy of someone" **means something that someone likes very much or is very interested in. 
 
 
• **Example**: Collecting antique coins is a fancy of his; he's been at it for years.
 
 
 
• **"Heart on the sleeve" **means to openly show one's feelings or emotions. 
 
 
• **Example**: She always wears her heart on her sleeve, so you always know how she's feeling.

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

Luckily, I managed to get a room in the college hostel, and I move in there.

options.text: Luckily, I managed to get a room

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option 1) i.e. 'and I move in there****'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

**__Key Points__**

 
• The **error in the sentence** lies in the use of the present tense **"move"** when it should be in the past tense "moved" to maintain consistency with the overall past tense narrative of the sentence.
 
• The **correct form **should be "and I moved in there," which would align with the past tense used in "managed to get a room."

Therefore, the correct answer is- '**and I move in there'.**

**Correct sentence: ***Luckily, I managed to get a room in the college hostel, **and I moved in there**. *
